You have never heard of this show. You just watched this whole clip (descriptions in brackets are what is on screen; speakers are described by how they look):
[On screen: Wide shot of the storm-lashed harbour, lanterns swinging on the quay.]
a figure in period dress: "Every wedding needs a widow. Why not two?"
[On screen: Close-up on the man in period dress's jaw tightening.]
a figure in period dress: "My father built this tower with his own hands."
[On screen: Low angle on the figure in period dress framed against the lighthouse beam.]
a man in period dress: "Your father paid me to watch over you."
[Sound: Glass shatters on stone.]
[On screen: Slow push-in on the man in period dress as the lamp flickers behind them.]
a figure in period dress: "Tell me the truth, or tell me nothing."
[On screen: Slow push-in on the widow as the lamp flickers behind them.]
[Action: the widow throws open the shutters; the storm floods in.]
a figure in period dress: "Order! I will have order in my hall!"
[On screen: Wide shot of the storm-lashed harbour, lanterns swinging on the quay.]
a figure in period dress: "Drink deep, little lamp-keeper."
[On screen: Close-up on the figure in period dress's hands gripping the rail.]
[Action: the figure in period dress draws a short blade from a boot.]
[On screen: High wide shot of the crowded hall turning toward the door.]
[Action: the the figure in period dress kneels on the slick quay boards.]
[On screen: High wide shot of the crowded hall turning toward the door.]
a man in period dress: "I saw who slipped the ring into your shawl."
[On screen: Tight shot on a silver ring glinting in candlelight.]
a figure in period dress: "Search her pockets. She is a thief!"
[On screen: Extreme close-up on the figure in period dress's eyes, wet with sea spray.]
a figure in period dress: "Every wedding needs a widow. Why not two?"
